title: Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres
short: QORL: a 4B model writes Postgres query plans
author: Rohan Bansal (independent; written at the Recurse Center)
more_note: Its interactive figures (the search-space counter, the calibration queue, the job-13b median draw, the reward formulas with notes on every term) are worth opening there; this page redraws only the results and the reward example, and recomputes the median draw exactly.

companion.t: Experiment 033 results (the repository's own analysis of the headline run)
companion.n: The author's analysis behind the 1.81x: how best-of-three was selected, the spread between repeated searches, and the caveats the post leaves out ("The 1.805x ratio is not an 80.5% latency reduction").

takeaway: On the 113 queries of the IMDb Join Order Benchmark, a 4B open model post-trained by one person for about $1,200 (LoRA SFT on about 400 GPT-6 Astra agent trajectories, then RL with a noise-aware reward) writes pg_hint_plan hints whose plans average 1.40x the speed of Postgres 18's own in one search (geometric mean); the headline 1.81x, or 44.7% less summed time, is the best of three searches picked by single timings, with the search time excluded and the planner at its default cost settings.
verdict: Believe the method and the measurement work: the noise rig, the reward fixes and the released code and per-query results are careful and honest, and the repository itself flags the caveats. Read 1.40x (one search) as the model's result and 1.81x as a search budget's: both on a benchmark watched during development, against Postgres with random_page_cost at its default 4.0 while the model often set 1.1, and with checkpoint differences smaller than the 1.33x to 1.47x spread between repeated searches.

headline.k: geometric-mean speedup of the model's own choice, 339 searches (113 JOB queries, three each)
headline.d: 19.1% less summed latency; three repetitions ranged 1.33x to 1.47x

headline.k: geometric mean and summed latency alike, one plan per query picked from up to 15 by a single timing each
headline.d: the same measurement as "44.7% latency reduction": 1 − 1/1.81; the search time is not counted
headline.at: we saw a 1.81x geometric mean speedup

headline.k: about $800 of 2 x H100 rental (about 95 hours) and $400 of API fees for the Astra demonstrations
headline.d: plus two RTX 3090s at home; development and evaluation on one desk machine

code.n: Harness, measurement, SFT and RL code, configs, every experiment's README and results, per-query results of the final run. No licence file; no weights or adapters released.

discussion.t: Hacker News: "Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres"

responses.t: The repository's results for the final run (experiment 033)
responses.n: Separates the model's choice (1.4048x), the within-search rule (1.4355x) and best-of-three (1.8054x); notes that 1.805x "is not an 80.5% latency reduction", that comparing it with a one-search SFT baseline "would mix policy improvement with additional search compute", that JOB "has been inspected during development", and that only 17 queries win in all three searches.

The model's favourite setting, random_page_cost=1.1, suggests the baseline's cost settings were not tuned for fast storage, which "could easily explain the difference by itself". The repository confirms the baseline ran at the default 4.0; no reply.

responses.t: An 8 GB in-memory dataset, warmed, read-only
responses.n: Warns of overfitting and asks whether the plans would hold at scale and on more realistic workloads; database statistics and workloads drift.

responses.t: Planning time is the constraint a live planner works under
responses.n: A real planner must minimise planning plus execution on live statistics, and the 95 hours of training and the search are outside the benchmark numbers. The post's own framing (repeated analytic queries) answers part of this.

responses.t: pg_hint_plan's debug log shows whether a hint was used
responses.n: Answering whether a hinted plan still computes the query: the hints only choose among plans for the same SQL, and the debug log was used during evaluation to confirm Postgres applied them. The author's only comment in the thread.
